title: Pipeline exec phase is a no-op stub
rationale: In `src/pipeline/orchestrator.ts:134-139`, the `exec` phase simply logs 'delegating to exec module' and continues with no actual execution. The comment says 'wired in T9' but the delegation was never implemented. A full `milhouse --run` pipeline will skip task execution entirely, making the orchestrator unable to complete its primary purpose.
symptom: Pipeline exec phase is a no-op stub
hypothesis: In `src/pipeline/orchestrator.ts:134-139`, the `exec` phase simply logs 'delegating to exec module' and continues with no actual execution. The comment says 'wired in T9' but the delegation was never implemented. A full `milhouse --run` pipeline will skip task execution entirely, making the orchestrator unable to complete its primary purpose.
strategy: Wire the exec phase to the existing execution infrastructure in `src/execution/`. Import the appropriate executor and invoke it with the run's tasks, passing through the runId, workDir, and config. Add cost tracking for the exec phase.

title: createRun mutates runs index without file locking
rationale: In `src/state/runs.ts:310-319`, `createRun()` calls `loadRunsIndex()`, mutates the array, then calls `saveRunsIndex()` without any file locking. Other concurrent-safe functions like `updateRunPhaseInMetaWithLock` and `saveRunsIndexWithLock` use proper locking. If two processes create runs simultaneously, one run entry could be lost due to the read-modify-write race condition.
symptom: createRun mutates runs index without file locking
hypothesis: In `src/state/runs.ts:310-319`, `createRun()` calls `loadRunsIndex()`, mutates the array, then calls `saveRunsIndex()` without any file locking. Other concurrent-safe functions like `updateRunPhaseInMetaWithLock` and `saveRunsIndexWithLock` use proper locking. If two processes create runs simultaneously, one run entry could be lost due to the read-modify-write race condition.
scope_impact: src/state/runs.ts — createRun(), also deleteRun() at line 330
strategy: Refactor `createRun()` to use `saveRunsIndexWithLock()` for the index update step. Similarly, refactor `deleteRun()` to use the locking mechanism. The run metadata write (separate file) is safe since it's a new unique file.

title: Run lock (acquireRunLock) has TOCTOU race condition
rationale: In `src/state/run-lock.ts:44-68`, `acquireRunLock` checks if the lock file exists with `existsSync`, reads it, checks the PID, then writes a new lock. Between the check and the write, another process could acquire the same lock. Unlike the file-lock mechanism used in `runs.ts` (which uses atomic operations), this lock uses a non-atomic check-then-write pattern.
symptom: Run lock (acquireRunLock) has TOCTOU race condition
hypothesis: In `src/state/run-lock.ts:44-68`, `acquireRunLock` checks if the lock file exists with `existsSync`, reads it, checks the PID, then writes a new lock. Between the check and the write, another process could acquire the same lock. Unlike the file-lock mechanism used in `runs.ts` (which uses atomic operations), this lock uses a non-atomic check-then-write pattern.
strategy: Replace the existsSync/readFileSync/writeFileSync pattern with an exclusive file creation approach (e.g., `writeFileSync` with `wx` flag which fails if file exists), or reuse the existing `withFileLock()` mechanism from `src/state/file-lock.ts`.

title: Stash pop failure silently ignored in BranchService
rationale: In `src/vcs/services/branch-service.ts:141-143` (success path) and `152-154` (error path), `git stash pop` results are not checked. If stash pop fails (e.g., merge conflicts with the new branch state), the user's stashed changes could be silently left in the stash. The user would not be informed that their changes were not restored.
symptom: Stash pop failure silently ignored in BranchService
hypothesis: In `src/vcs/services/branch-service.ts:141-143` (success path) and `152-154` (error path), `git stash pop` results are not checked. If stash pop fails (e.g., merge conflicts with the new branch state), the user's stashed changes could be silently left in the stash. The user would not be informed that their changes were not restored.
strategy: Check the result of `runGitCommand(['stash', 'pop'], workDir)` and log a warning or return an error-with-context if it fails. At minimum, surface a warning so the user knows to manually apply their stash.

title: clearEngineRateLimiters uses Promise.all instead of Promise.allSettled
rationale: In `src/engines/middleware/rate-limit.ts:155-162`, `clearEngineRateLimiters()` uses `Promise.all()` to stop all limiters. If any `limiter.stop()` throws, the remaining limiters won't be stopped and `engineLimiters.clear()` may leave zombie entries. The same pattern exists in `RateLimiterGroup.stopAll()` at lines 244-249.
symptom: clearEngineRateLimiters uses Promise.all instead of Promise.allSettled
hypothesis: In `src/engines/middleware/rate-limit.ts:155-162`, `clearEngineRateLimiters()` uses `Promise.all()` to stop all limiters. If any `limiter.stop()` throws, the remaining limiters won't be stopped and `engineLimiters.clear()` may leave zombie entries. The same pattern exists in `RateLimiterGroup.stopAll()` at lines 244-249.
strategy: Replace `Promise.all()` with `Promise.allSettled()` in both functions to ensure all limiters are stopped regardless of individual failures. Log any failures for observability.

title: ProgressiveTimeoutState.reset() does not restore initial timeout
rationale: In `src/engines/middleware/timeout.ts:173`, the `reset()` method computes `this.currentTimeout = this.maxTimeout / this.multiplier ** 3` instead of restoring to the original `initialTimeout`. This formula only equals `initialTimeout` when `multiplier^3` happens to be the correct ratio, which is coincidental. After a success, the progressive timeout resets to an unpredictable value rather than the configured starting point.
symptom: ProgressiveTimeoutState.reset() does not restore initial timeout
hypothesis: In `src/engines/middleware/timeout.ts:173`, the `reset()` method computes `this.currentTimeout = this.maxTimeout / this.multiplier ** 3` instead of restoring to the original `initialTimeout`. This formula only equals `initialTimeout` when `multiplier^3` happens to be the correct ratio, which is coincidental. After a success, the progressive timeout resets to an unpredictable value rather than the configured starting point.
strategy: Store `initialTimeout` in the constructor and use it in `reset()`: `this.currentTimeout = this.initialTimeout`.

title: PrService emits misleading event names for non-branch-create operations
rationale: In `src/vcs/services/pr-service.ts`, the `git:branch:create` event is emitted for branch pushes (line 96: `pushed:${branch}`), PR creation failures (line 171: `pr-failed:${branch}`), and PR creation success (line 181: `pr-created:${branch}`). Using the same event name with a prefixed payload makes it impossible to distinguish operations via event handlers and makes debugging harder.
symptom: PrService emits misleading event names for non-branch-create operations
hypothesis: In `src/vcs/services/pr-service.ts`, the `git:branch:create` event is emitted for branch pushes (line 96: `pushed:${branch}`), PR creation failures (line 171: `pr-failed:${branch}`), and PR creation success (line 181: `pr-created:${branch}`). Using the same event name with a prefixed payload makes it impossible to distinguish operations via event handlers and makes debugging harder.
strategy: Introduce distinct event names: `git:branch:push`, `git:pr:create`, `git:pr:failed`. Update any event listeners accordingly.

title: Default engine timeout of 66 minutes may mask hung processes
rationale: In `src/engines/middleware/timeout.ts:45`, the default timeout is `4000000`ms (~66 minutes). While LLM operations can be slow, this extremely high default means a stuck engine process won't be detected for over an hour. Most LLM calls complete within a few minutes, and a 66-minute timeout provides almost no protection against hangs.
symptom: Default engine timeout of 66 minutes may mask hung processes
hypothesis: In `src/engines/middleware/timeout.ts:45`, the default timeout is `4000000`ms (~66 minutes). While LLM operations can be slow, this extremely high default means a stuck engine process won't be detected for over an hour. Most LLM calls complete within a few minutes, and a 66-minute timeout provides almost no protection against hangs.
strategy: Lower the default timeout to a more reasonable value (e.g., 600000ms / 10 minutes) and allow per-phase or per-engine overrides via ResolvedConfig. Document the timeout configuration for operators.

title: loadRunMeta uses unsafe `null as unknown as RunMeta` default
rationale: In `src/state/runs.ts:174`, `loadRunMeta` passes `null as unknown as RunMeta` as the default value to `loadJsonFile`. If the file exists but parsing fails, `loadJsonFile` returns this type-punned null as if it were a valid `RunMeta`. The function signature says it returns `RunMeta | null`, but callers may not be aware that a parsed-but-invalid file also produces null. The same pattern appears in `src/state/probes.ts`.
symptom: loadRunMeta uses unsafe `null as unknown as RunMeta` default
hypothesis: In `src/state/runs.ts:174`, `loadRunMeta` passes `null as unknown as RunMeta` as the default value to `loadJsonFile`. If the file exists but parsing fails, `loadJsonFile` returns this type-punned null as if it were a valid `RunMeta`. The function signature says it returns `RunMeta | null`, but callers may not be aware that a parsed-but-invalid file also produces null. The same pattern appears in `src/state/probes.ts`.
strategy: Refactor `loadJsonFile` to accept `null` as a valid default by making its generic type `T | null`, or create a separate `loadJsonFileOrNull` variant that explicitly handles the null case without type casting.

title: Diff analyzer uses hardcoded 500-line threshold for large file detection
rationale: In `src/gates/diff/analyzer.ts:26`, the large file threshold is hardcoded as `changes > 500`. This is not configurable, which means it can't be adjusted for projects where larger diffs are expected (e.g., generated code, migrations). The hygiene score deduction for large files (line 148) is also hardcoded.

hypothesis: In `src/gates/diff/analyzer.ts:26`, the large file threshold is hardcoded as `changes > 500`. The hygiene score deduction for large files (line 148) is also hardcoded.
strategy: Accept a configuration parameter for the large file threshold and hygiene score weights, either via function arguments or through the gate configuration system.

title: Duplicate in-memory lock pattern across run state functions
rationale: In `src/state/runs.ts`, the in-memory lock pattern (wait-for-promise, create new promise, try/finally release) is repeated identically in `updateRunMetaWithLock` (lines 460-491), `updateRunPhaseInMetaWithLock` (lines 497-543), and `saveRunsIndexWithLock` (lines 566-594). Each uses the same structure with different lock variables (`runMetaLockPromise`, `runsIndexLockPromise`).
symptom: Duplicate in-memory lock pattern across run state functions
hypothesis: In `src/state/runs.ts`, the in-memory lock pattern (wait-for-promise, create new promise, try/finally release) is repeated identically in `updateRunMetaWithLock` (lines 460-491), `updateRunPhaseInMetaWithLock` (lines 497-543), and `saveRunsIndexWithLock` (lines 566-594). Each uses the same structure with different lock variables (`runMetaLockPromise`, `runsIndexLockPromise`).
strategy: Extract a generic `withInMemoryLock(lockRef, fn)` helper that encapsulates the wait/acquire/release pattern. Replace the three inline implementations with calls to this helper.
